title: Chat event watermarking and idempotent sink patterns for Python SDK streaming
creator: Lena Zhou
description:
Problem:
Teams building streaming chat integrations need a robust, easy-to-use pattern for handling interleaved events (tokens, tool calls, function results, metadata) without duplicating side effects when reconnects or retries occur. Current SDK streaming primitives make it easy to iterate tokens but do not provide a canonical approach for: ordering across event types, detecting duplicate events after reconnects, and aligning user-side sinks (databases, message queues) to be idempotent and low-latency.

Proposal summary:
Introduce a lightweight watermarking + idempotent-sink pattern in the Python SDK that: (1) surfaces a stable event identifier (event_id) and monotonic sequence number (seq) per stream; (2) emits periodic watermark events indicating a durable progress checkpoint; and (3) provides an example idempotent sink helper (IdempotentSink) users can reuse to safely persist events across reconnects and retries. The SDK will expose ergonomic streaming primitives (sync & async) that include event metadata needed for this pattern and examples for common sinks (Postgres upsert, Kafka-unique-key, Redis dedupe).

Design details:
- Event envelope: every streaming event will include flattened metadata fields: event_id (uuid string), seq (integer incrementing from 1 for the session), event_type (token|tool_call|tool_result|watermark|finish), and durable (boolean indicates if content is safe to persist).
- Watermarks: server-side will emit watermark events with seq and commit_offset. Watermarks represent points where upstream has persisted or is guaranteed to have emitted all earlier events. Clients can use watermarks to garbage collect local buffers and advance sinks.
- IdempotentSink helper: a small abstraction with methods: .prepare(event_id, key), .commit(event_id), .is_committed(event_id). Example implementations will show using a single-row lock + upsert in Postgres and an idempotent publish for Kafka (idempotent producer + dedupe key).
- API ergonomics: provide two primary entry points: (A) sync iterator: for event in client.stream_chat(...): process(event); (B) async async for event in client.stream_chat_async(...): process(event). Events are plain dataclasses (ChatEvent) but exported as simple dicts to avoid deep dependency on dataclasses. The event dict includes the metadata described above.
- Retry semantics: when reconnects happen, server will attempt to resume from last known seq if provided. Client will automatically pass last_committed_seq (if using IdempotentSink or explicit checkpoint) so server can resume at next seq. This reduces duplicated durable events.
- Backpressure guidance: SDK will document recommended patterns: buffer watermarks, prefer writing only durable events, batch upserts between watermarks, and use the IdempotentSink.commit hooked to watermark to mark progress.

Example usage (sync):

from redwood import RedwoodClient

client = RedwoodClient(api_key=... )

sink = IdempotentSink.postgres(dsn="postgres://...", table="chat_events")

for event in client.stream_chat(session_id="s-123", prompt="..."):
    # event is a dict with keys: event_id, seq, event_type, durable, payload
    if event["event_type"] == "token":
        # display token incrementally, don't persist tokens by default
        ui.write(event["payload"])
    elif event["event_type"] == "tool_result":
        # persist tool results (durable) using idempotent sink
        if event["durable"]:
            sink.prepare(event["event_id"], key=event["payload"]["id"])
            sink.upsert(event["event_id"], row=event["payload"])
    elif event["event_type"] == "watermark":
        # watermark: durable checkpoint we can commit to avoid reprocessing
        sink.commit(event["seq"])

Example usage (async):

async with client.stream_chat_async(session_id="s-123") as stream:
    async for event in stream:
        # same handling as sync example, but await sink ops where needed
        ...

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests to validate IdempotentSink implementations (simulate duplicate event deliveries and out-of-order seq).
- Integration test bridging a small local Postgres instance and a mocked server to validate resume semantics using last_committed_seq.
- E2E with service staging: ensure watermark events are emitted and client resume preserves no duplicate durable writes when last_committed_seq is supplied.

Telemetry & metrics:
- watermark_lag_seconds (gauge): server-side and client-side lag between latest seq and last_committed_seq.
- stream_reconnects_total (counter) per session and reason.
- durable_event_duplicates_total (counter) to catch regressions in idempotency guarantees.
- sink_commit_latency_ms (histogram) for common sinks.

Backwards compatibility & rollout:
- The event envelope adds event_id & seq but keeps existing token payload shapes. Default SDK behavior will not require users to adopt IdempotentSink; pattern is opt-in.
- Feature flag the watermark + resume headers in client; rollout to 10% then 50% then 100% while validating metrics.

Docs & examples:
- New doc page under SDK Streaming: "Watermarks & idempotent sinks" with full code samples, migration guidance, and checklist for common sinks.
- Cookbook entry: "How to persist tool results safely from a streaming chat" with Postgres/Kafka/Redis recipes.

Trade-offs and alternatives considered:
- Server-only dedupe: rejected because many side effects are performed by users (DB writes, external calls) and must be controlled client-side.
- Relying on event timestamps: rejected because clocks and ordering across multi-region paths are brittle. Sequence numbers + watermarks are simpler and deterministic.

Open questions:
- How large should a session seq be (32-bit vs 64-bit)? Proposal: 64-bit to avoid wraparound for very long sessions.
- Should we expose a high-level sink that also batches automatically? We'd provide an example but keep the core helper minimal to avoid opinionation across customer infra.

Risks:
- Misused IdempotentSink patterns could cause increased latency if naive locking/upsert is used. We'll include guidance and examples tuned for high throughput (batched upserts between watermarks).
acceptance_criteria: SDK emits event_id and seq fields for streaming chat events
Server emits periodic watermark events and client exposes them to callers
IdempotentSink helper is implemented with Postgres and Kafka examples
Unit and integration tests cover duplicate and resume scenarios
Docs and cookbook published with sample code and migration steps
Telemetry added for watermark lag, reconnects, and duplicate durables
